segments.t: Barinov is still angry with the judge who took away his licence, and he and the cook Senya have a plan for her birthday dinner. Senya has brought a strong "remedy", and the chef wants to know exactly what it does. Here's the Russian first.
Сеня, ты принёс то особое средство?
Да, шеф, это сильное средство.
Это вообще новое мощное лекарство.
Как быстро оно начинает действовать?
Очень быстро, шеф, буквально сразу.
Одна таблетка решает все ваши проблемы.
И какой будет точный эффект?
Обещаю, клиент от унитаза не отойдёт!
Отлично, судья запомнит этот юбилей!
Мы добавим таблетку в её суп?
Нет, положим порошок прямо на гуся.
Главное, чтобы другие гости не отравились.
Не бойся, я сделаю всё лично.
Let's follow the plan.
Сеня, ты принёс то особое средство?
'Senya, did you bring that special remedy?' "Prinyos", brought, is a man's past of "prinesti", to carry here. "To osoboye sredstvo" is "that special means", and "sredstvo" is any means or remedy.
Да, шеф, это сильное средство.
'Yes, chef, this is a strong remedy.' "Sil'noye", strong, is "sila", strength, made into an adjective. It ends in -oye because "sredstvo" is neuter.
Это вообще новое мощное лекарство.
'This is brand new powerful medicine.' "Voobshche novoye" is "totally new". "Moshchnoye", powerful, is from "moshch'", power, and "lekarstvo" is a drug from the pharmacy.
Как быстро оно начинает действовать?
'How quickly does it start to act?' "Nachinayet deystvovat'" is "begins to act", from "deystviye", action. "Ono", it, is neuter to match the medicine.
Очень быстро, шеф, буквально сразу.
'Very quickly, chef, literally right away.' "Bukval'no", literally, has "bukva", a letter, inside it, just as "literally" has "letter". "Srazu" is "at once".
Одна таблетка решает все ваши проблемы.
'One pill solves all your problems.' "Odna" is feminine because "tabletka", pill, is. "Reshayet" is "solves", and "vse vashi problemy" is "all your problems".
И какой будет точный эффект?

'And what will be the exact effect?' Masculine to match "effekt", "kakoy" asks "what kind of". "Budet", will be, is all the future needs here, and "tochnyy", exact, is the adjective behind the familiar "tochno".
Обещаю, клиент от унитаза не отойдёт!
'I promise, the customer will not leave the toilet!' "Ne otoydyot ot" is "won't step away from", and after "ot" the word becomes "unitaza". "Obeshchayu" is "I promise".
Отлично, судья запомнит этот юбилей!
'Excellent, the judge will remember this anniversary!' "Zapomnit" is "will remember", with "za-" for fixing it in memory. "Yubiley" is a round-number birthday or anniversary.
Мы добавим таблетку в её суп?
'Shall we add the pill into her soup?' "Dobavim" is "we'll add". "Yeyo", her, never changes its ending, and "v sup" is "into the soup".
Нет, положим порошок прямо на гуся.
'No, we will put the powder directly on the goose.' "Polozhim" is "we'll lay", for putting something down flat. "Poroshok" is "powder", and "na gusya" is "onto the goose".
Главное, чтобы другие гости не отравились.
'The main thing is that other guests do not get poisoned.' "Glavnoye, chtoby" is "the main thing, so that". "Otravilis'", got poisoned, ends in -lis', and it follows "chtoby" in the past form.
Не бойся, я сделаю всё лично.

'Do not fear, I will do everything personally.' "Ne boysya" is the "ty" command "don't be afraid". "Lichno" is "personally", and "sdelayu vsyo" is "I'll do everything". Now let's listen to the whole conversation again from start to finish.
